items.summary: ### Summary An architectural security boundary bypass in inline-detach and MessageInspector allows remote, unauthenticated attackers to force unbounded recursive decompression routines. DOMShell: domshell_eval classified as read-tier can execute side-effecting JavaScript without --allow-write
items.summary: ### Summary The `domshell_eval` MCP tool (and the `eval` command inside `domshell_execute`) was classified as **read-tier**, allowing it to run without the `--allow-write` server flag. However, `eval` and the write-tier `js` command dispatch to the same handler in the extension and call CDP `Runtime.evaluate` with the raw expression string and no side-effect gate. items.title: djangocms-moderation: Moderation comments disclosed to non-participant staff via the admin changelist
items.summary: ## Summary The Django admin views for moderation comments (`CollectionCommentAdmin` and `RequestCommentAdmin`) render the full comment body but scope access only by an attacker-controlled `id` in the URL and Django's model-level `view_*comment` permission. They perform no per-object participant check. As a result, any authenticated staff user who holds the comment *view* permission can read the comments of **any** collection or moderation request — including ones they are not a participant of —

items.title: Mareforma: Unsigned Claims Can Be Promoted to REPLICATED via Missing Signature Enforcement in Convergence Path
items.summary: ### Summary `mareforma` 0.3.3 contains a critical integrity flaw in the REPLICATED convergence logic (`_maybe_update_replicated_unlocked()` in `mareforma/db/core.py:1300-1319`). The peer-selection SQL query that determines whether two independent claims "agree" on the same anchor does not verify that either claim carries a valid cryptographic signature from an enrolled validator key. items.title: Mareforma: transparency_logged trusts the unsigned rekor block
items.summary: ## What's wrong During restore, `transparency_logged` is recomputed as `1 if (toml_logged is not False and bundle_has_rekor) else 0`, where `bundle_has_rekor` comes only from a `rekor.uuid` field inside `signature_bundle`. That derivation is wrong in both directions. First, the rekor block is metadata attached after signing (`attach_rekor_entry` in `mareforma/signing/rekor.py` leaves the payload and signatures untouched), so it is not covered by the Ed25519 signature.
